title: 1952 AHSME Problem 44
statement: If an integer of two digits is \(k\) times the sum of its digits, the number formed by interchanging the digits is the sum of the digits multiplied by:

solutions.text:
Let the original number be \(10a+b=k(a+b).\) The reversed number is \(10b+a.\) Since \[ \begin{gathered} (10a+b)+(10b+a) \\ =11(a+b), \end{gathered} \] the reversed number equals \[ \begin{aligned} &11(a+b)-k(a+b)\\ &\qquad=(11-k)(a+b). \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let the two digits be \(a\) and \(b\), and express both the original and reversed numbers
